title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self

questions.question: In the comparison, what was the first servant told to do with the small amount of money?
questions.answer: He was told to buy clothes from a certain kind of cloth.

questions.question: What extra thing was put in the second servant’s pocket besides the money?
questions.answer: A written note about a task he needed to do.

questions.question: Why would a wise person know that the larger amount of money was not mainly for buying clothes?
questions.answer: Because a very nice outfit had already been bought with much less money, so the bigger amount had to be for a more important purpose.

questions.question: What mistake did the second servant make before spending the money?
questions.answer: He did not read the note that explained what he was supposed to do.

questions.question: What did the second servant do after looking at the first servant?
questions.answer: He copied him and spent all the money on clothing.

questions.question: How was the clothing bought by the second servant described compared with the first servant’s?
questions.answer: It was much poorer and far worse.

questions.question: How did the employer respond to the second servant’s action?
questions.answer: He strongly scolded him and punished him.

questions.question: What lesson does the comparison teach about human abilities and life?
questions.answer: Our abilities were not given just for bodily pleasure and worldly living; they were given for a higher purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens if a person uses life only like an animal?
questions.answer: That person falls lower than animals even though he was given much more.

questions.question: What warning is given to the nafs and the friend at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They are warned not to waste life’s gifts on short-lived desires.

questions.question: How much money did the first servant receive, and what was it for?
questions.answer: He received twenty gold pieces to have clothing made.

questions.question: How much money did the second servant receive?
questions.answer: He received one thousand gold pieces.

questions.question: What does the huge difference in the two amounts suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the second servant had a much bigger and more important duty.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done first after receiving the note and the money?
questions.answer: He should have read the note and followed its instructions.

questions.question: Why was it foolish for the second servant to spend everything on clothes?
questions.answer: Because he ignored the real job he had been sent to do.

questions.question: What caused the second servant to choose the wrong action?
questions.answer: He followed what another servant did instead of understanding his own assignment.

questions.question: In the lesson after the comparison, what does “capital” of life mean?
questions.answer: It means the valuable abilities and opportunities given to a person.

questions.question: What are people told not to spend this life capital on?
questions.answer: They are told not to waste it on bodily cravings and temporary worldly fun.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can a human become worse than an animal?
questions.answer: By using great human gifts only for low desires.

questions.question: What is the main point of the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Human powers were not created only to gain worldly comfort like animals.

questions.question: What did the first servant manage to buy with only a little money?
questions.answer: A very nice set of clothes.

questions.question: What shows that the second servant had a special mission besides spending money?
questions.answer: He was sent with a written message and a large amount of money to handle some business.

questions.question: What important clue did the second servant ignore?
questions.answer: He ignored the written instructions in his pocket.

questions.question: Why is the employer’s anger understandable in the story?
questions.answer: Because the servant wasted a large trust and failed to do the job he was sent for.

questions.question: In the warning section, who is being spoken to?
questions.answer: The person’s lower self and close companion are being addressed.

questions.question: What kind of pleasures are mentioned as unworthy goals for human life?
questions.answer: Physical pleasures and short-lasting worldly enjoyments.

questions.question: What comparison is made between humans and animals in the final lines?
questions.answer: Humans have been given much greater resources, but if they misuse them, they can sink much lower.

questions.question: What is one good summary sentence for the whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah gave humans great gifts for a noble purpose, so they should not waste them on low desires.

questions.question: In the story, what was the first servant’s task connected to?
questions.answer: It was connected to getting clothes made.

questions.question: What made the second servant’s situation different from the first servant’s?
questions.answer: He was given far more money and a written instruction for another job.

questions.question: What should people understand from the fact that twenty coins were enough for excellent clothes?
questions.answer: They should understand that the much larger amount was meant for something beyond clothing.

questions.question: What bad decision did the second servant make with the shopkeeper?
questions.answer: He handed over all the money for an outfit.

questions.question: What result did the second servant get from that bad decision?
questions.answer: He ended up with low-quality clothing.

questions.question: What does the note in his pocket stand for in the lesson of the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for the guidance a person is supposed to follow in life.

questions.question: What does the passage tell a person to do instead of living only for worldly enjoyment?
questions.answer: A person should wake up, use life wisely, and not waste its gifts on passing desires.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a human can fall below animals?
questions.answer: Because humans have higher abilities and greater responsibility, so misusing them is a bigger failure.

questions.question: What word best describes worldly life in the final warning: lasting or temporary?
questions.answer: Temporary.

questions.question: What is the moral of the comparison in simple words?
questions.answer: Don’t waste the precious gifts of life on small and passing things.

questions.question: Who gave the servants money in the comparison?
questions.answer: Their employer did.

questions.question: What was placed in the second servant’s pocket along with the money?
questions.answer: A paper with instructions.

questions.question: What does the comparison ask the reader to understand about human faculties?
questions.answer: They were not given just to live for this world like animals do.

questions.question: How do we know the second servant misunderstood his duty?
questions.answer: He used all the money for clothing instead of doing the business he had been sent for.

questions.question: What was wrong with the quality of the clothes he bought?
questions.answer: They were poor and much worse than the other servant’s.

questions.question: What does the employer’s punishment tell us about responsibility?
questions.answer: It shows that wasting an important trust is a serious wrong.

questions.question: In the direct advice after the story, what should a person not do with life’s abilities?
questions.answer: A person should not use them only for bodily pleasure and short-lived worldly things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human beings compared with the best animal?
questions.answer: Humans have been given far greater wealth in abilities.

questions.question: If a human wastes those greater gifts, where can he fall compared with the lowest animal?
questions.answer: He can fall even lower.

questions.question: At the start of the target passage, what are readers told to notice through the comparison?
questions.answer: They are told to see that human abilities have a higher purpose than animal-like worldly living.

questions.question: What did the first servant do successfully with the money he was given?
questions.answer: He bought a high-quality outfit.

questions.question: What two things did the second servant receive from his employer?
questions.answer: A large amount of money and a written message.

questions.question: What should the second servant have realized from receiving much more money than the first servant?
questions.answer: He should have realized he was meant to carry out a more important task.

questions.question: Instead of understanding his own job, whose action did the second servant copy?
questions.answer: He copied the first servant.

questions.question: Why was the second servant’s choice not only wrong but also senseless?
questions.answer: Because he ignored clear guidance and used a great resource for a small purpose.

questions.question: In the warning, what parts of human life are called “capital and potentialities”?
questions.answer: A person’s valuable life resources and abilities.

questions.question: What kind of life is criticized in the last paragraph of the target passage?
questions.answer: A life spent chasing bodily desires and temporary pleasures.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying a person may become lower than an animal?
questions.answer: It means he misuses his higher gifts so badly that he fails beneath creatures with fewer abilities.

questions.question: What should a Muslim student learn from this whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah gave us special abilities for meaningful and higher goals, so we should use them wisely and not waste them on passing desires.
